title: Three-slide seller blitz lab (prototype)
content:
Purpose: 3-slide flash deck sellers can use in 60–90s technical intro or as a leave-behind after an early pilot conversation. Extremely compact: value (slide 1), ops/assertion+fallback (slide 2), quick pilot checklist + win criteria (slide 3).

Slide 1 — "Value in 30s" (Speaker notes)
- Headline: Ship LLM features with predictable latency, cost, and fallbacks.
- 3 bullets for story:
  1) "Latency-first runtime" — continuous batching + kernel selection = predictable p99 for chat flows. How this matters: fewer thread-blocking surprises for product demos.
  2) "Cost controls you can tune" — caching, quantization recommendations, routing policies. One-line example: 20% token cost reduction using prefix caching on customer summaries.
  3) "Deploy where you need it" — hosted for speed, dedicated for throughput, private for regulated data.
- Quick metric strip (one-liners): typical demo config = 1–2x latency vs open-hosted baseline; reserved can cut per-call cost by ~35% at scale.
- Speaker cue: use a customer-analogy: "Think of Redwood like a CDN for model calls: predictable, configurable, and with fallbacks so your app stays live."

Slide 2 — "Ops & Fallbacks (rapid reassurance)" (Speaker notes)
- One-line setup: Customers worry about outages, model regressions, and runaway costs. This slide is a rapid rebuttal.
- Left column — Runtime guarantees (two bullets):
  * Autoscaling + reserved pool option for steady throughput. SLA-backed tiers available.
  * Smart routing w/ automatic fallback to lower-latency / cheaper model variants when capacity constrained.
- Right column — Quick fallback examples (script snippets for SE):
  * Fallback pattern: route chat -> if token budget exceeds threshold then switch to quantized model variant; send ‘degraded but safe’ UI message to user. (One-sentence code idea: header X-Model-Fallback: quant-1).
  * Canary rollout + immediate rollback: explain canary % and automatic QoS threshold for rollbacks.
- Objections & one-liners:
  * "What if output quality drops?" — answer: canary + evals on prompt set; automatic regression alerting.
  * "Will this add work to my infra?" — answer: single API; we manage routing and runtime; integrated observability hooks for your SREs.
- Speaker cue: keep responses tight; hand the SE the next slide pilot checklist if they ask for how to start.

Slide 3 — "Pilot checklist: win in 2 weeks" (Speaker notes)
- Goal: move from initial integration to usable metrics and a go/no-go decision.
- Minimal pilot scope (bulleted checklist):
  1) Define 3 core prompts / flows (3–5 test cases each) — owner: product/PM.
  2) Pick success metric(s) — latency (p50/p95), cost per 1K requests, and subjective quality score from 10 internal reviews.
  3) Integration skeleton — one route to Redwood API using short token and streaming. Triage doc + example snippet attached.
  4) Fallback policy — pick one route (quantized variant or region fallback) to enable during pilot.
  5) Data & compliance check — decide whether to use hosted (default) or private (if regulated).
- Quick timeline (2-week cadence): Week 0: integrate + smoke test; Week 1: baseline traffic + collect metrics; Week 2: evaluate, decide expand/reserved.
- Success criteria (example): achieve p95 latency < 400ms on chat sample set AND cost projection < target threshold OR quality rating >= 8/10.
- Red flags and quick mitigations:
  * Red flag: token cost > proj -> mitigation: enable prefix caching and re-run perf sample.
  * Red flag: quality regression on canary -> mitigation: rollback to previous model and open regression ticket + apply prompt-specific guardrail.
- Leave-behind micro-asks for buyer:
  1) "Agree on 3 test prompts" (15 min)
  2) "Set target SLOs for pilot" (10 min)
  3) "Name an ops contact for autoscaling conversations" (5 min)

Appendix (notes for seller/SE) — internal quick tips (freeform, not for customer):
- Keep demo prompts short — long contexts balloon token cost.
- Use the "demo throttle" header to simulate production concurrency during demo.
- If asked about benchmarking: reference our public model catalog page; bring up recent benchmark numbers for the model family you're proposing.
- TODOs (internal): add one-line example cURL for fallback header; link to new pilot template (Confluence) — currently WIP.
- Open questions: what is smallest reserved commit we can offer for midmarket pilot accounts (tagging finance ops for answer).

Speaker rehearsal cues (bullet list):
- 0–15s: rapid headline + value (slide 1).
- 15–45s: address ops fear upfront (slide 2).
- 45–90s: propose pilot (slide 3) and get micro-ask.

Notes on usage:
- Intended recipients: field SEs + AE early-stage conversations. Keep as living doc; iterate based on pilot wins.
- Related assets to attach when we convert to slides: sample prompt set CSV, cURL snippets, pilot onboarding Confluence link, 1-page SLO calculator sheet.

Hard constraints for conversion to real deck:
- Do not include any customer logos in slide prototype until pilot permission granted.
- Make sure the pilot checklist has clear ownership per bullet.

End of prototype.

"Happy to iterate on tone (snappier vs formal) — current is intentionally conversational for SEs to riff from."
